correctness.rationale: Coordinate exchangeability gives mean alpha/n and pair moment rho=(beta−n)/(n(n−1)), yielding n−1 contrast eigenvalues 1−rho plus the exact 2×2 block eigenvalues. G=I iff alpha=0 and beta=n. Writing positive shell signed sums a,−b gives ab=n and a*C(n,(n−a)/2)=b*C(n,(n−b)/2). The exact consecutive-binomial ratio and paired-factor identity show for positive allowable a<=b that equality occurs iff b−a=0 or 2; hence n=s² or d(d+2) and only the listed shell pairs. The two-point third moment ab(a−b) yields exact cubic Walsh defect. Independent symbolic paired-factor identity and exhaustive exact shell-pair enumeration to n=100 corroborate the infinite argument.
residual_risks: The balanced square-dimensional 3-wise independent antipodal shells are already known from earlier quadratic-Walsh Gram work; only whole two-shell classification and near-square asymmetric cases count as novel.
Older weighted relative t-design and exchangeable orthogonal array literature may have equivalent two-shell all-n arithmetic classifications not in indexed searches.
Exhaustive n<=100 computation is corroboration, not universal proof; exact positive ratio-product inequality is required.
